reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general entropy stabilization and HEA properties but provides no specific support for the key premises about local lattice distortions, selective elemental segregation to surfaces, or their effect on premelting behavior in nanoparticles.
premises: High configurational entropy creates non-uniform bonding environments and local lattice distortions in HEA nanoparticles
These distortions promote selective segregation of lower-cohesive-energy elements to the nanoparticle surface
Surface segregation of lower-cohesive-energy elements lowers the energy barrier for surface premelting
Lower-entropy nanoparticles (binary/ternary) form more uniform surfaces with higher effective melting points
HEA nanoparticles will therefore exhibit a lower onset temperature for surface premelting compared to lower-entropy analogues
